subject: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s impacting FinApps payments - network triage
messages:
From: Claire Bennett <claire@finapps.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting live payments

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sustained increase in 5xx and 429 responses to Redwood hosted endpoints starting ~09:00 PST this morning. Our payments pipeline is sensitive — throughput has dropped ~30% and our retry logic is amplifying the load which is causing additional downstream timeouts. Key observations from our side: 
- 5xx rate ~15% for generation requests to model redwood-4b-prd
- 429 rate ~10% with bursty spikes tied to a retry loop in our jobs
- Retries show many connections resetting mid-handshake (RST), and our networking team suspects SNAT port exhaustion or firewall state limits on the path to Redwood.

This is customer-impacting and we need Redwood to triage immediately. Can you escalate and loop in SRE / networking leadership? We can share logs (attached) and are available on Slack/phone.

Attached: finapps_error_sample.log (samples, timestamps, request ids)

Thanks,
Claire Bennett
Head of Platform, FinApps
claire@finapps.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting FinApps payments

Forwarding FinApps incident — they report spike in 5xx/429s and believe there may be NAT/firewall limits on the path. Customer is seeing retries leading to throughput collapse.

Requesting triage and a short mitigation plan (15-30m) we can present to the customer. Also need recommended rollback/cleanup steps. Please treat as P0 and update me on the ETA.

Attaching customer impact snapshot for reference.
Attachment: customer-sla-impact.csv

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:03:34 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting FinApps payments

Vanessa / team,

Prelim triage from the edge and routing plane: we are seeing a traffic pattern consistent with SNAT port exhaustion on the customer side combined with intermittent TCP resets across the VPC peering path. Summary: 
- Edge logs show elevated connection reset counts (RST) for flows originating from FinApps public NAT IP ranges between 08:58–09:15 PST.
- Our connection tracking on the egress gateways shows short-lived half-open sessions and sudden port churn for the same source IPs.
- There are correlated retries from FinApps (client-side) that create an amplification effect; request concurrency spikes, connections reuse fails, and some flows land on alternate peering tunnels where firewall conntrack limits are more constrained.

Likely root causes (candidate): 
1) Customer NAT gateway exhausting ephemeral ports under retry amplification.
2) Firewall/conntrack limits on their peering path (or a middlebox with low conntrack table).
3) Asymmetric path routing to different Redwood edge clusters that have different conntrack headroom, producing intermittent 5xx.

Immediate mitigations we can enact (short-term):
- Route FinApps traffic to hosted fallback pool in us-west-2 (hosted API cluster) to avoid their peering path (requires account exec + customer approval).
- Apply a temporary rate-limit on request concurrency for the FinApps account at the edge (throttle bursts) to reduce port churn and allow their NAT to recover.
- Ask FinApps to increase conntrack table / NAT port ranges and patch their retry backoff to avoid immediate re-amplification.

I attached a short connection summary and opened SUP-1924 to track work. If we will change their routing, we need exec sign-off (this has potential billing/SL implications).

Attachment: redwood_edge_conn_summary.txt
Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/SUP-1924

I'll start with a temp throttle on our side and monitor; please confirm if we can proceed with reroute.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:45:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting FinApps payments

Thanks Sean — quick customer context: FinApps is in the middle of a midnight batch that is time-sensitive (payments settlement). They are anxious and tracking this with execs. They are open to a short maintenance window and appreciate transparent next steps.

Customer asks asked previously: if outage extends beyond 2 hours they expect a goodwill credit. We should be prepared to offer a defined compensation if the mitigation doesn't fully restore throughput.

Requested next steps I can communicate to FinApps now: 
- Redwood will apply a temporary burst throttle to reduce amplification (we need to confirm exact throttling rate).
- If not resolved within 30–45m, Redwood will re-route traffic to hosted fallback cluster (requires customer approval).

Vanessa — can you confirm whether you have authority to accept the reroute for them, or do you need exec (VP/CRO) approval?

Marissa
Principal Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Bennett <claire@finapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 11:05:48 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting FinApps payments

Hi Claire — quick update and a proposed short mitigation plan.

What we see: Redwood SREs identified a likely NAT/conntrack exhaustion + asymmetric peering that is triggering resets and downstream 5xx responses. Sean has applied a temporary soft throttle at the edge to limit burst concurrency and give your NAT a chance to clear ephemeral ports. Please note this is non-disruptive and should reduce immediate retries.

Proposed immediate action (requires your OK):
1) If the throttle doesn't restore normal rates within 30–45 minutes, we request permission to temporarily route your traffic to our hosted fallback cluster in us-west-2 for the next 2 hours. This reroute is transparent but may change how logs appear (different egress IPs) and will bypass your peering path.
2) FinApps should open/confirm a ticket with your networking team to increase NAT ephemeral port space and raise conntrack limits on any firewall appliances on the peering path.

Please reply with APPROVE to the reroute if you'd like us to proceed automatically after the 45m observation window, or DECLINE and we will continue with throttles and further diagnostics. If you prefer a phone call, I'm available now.

Thanks — we are treating this with priority and will keep you updated every 15 minutes.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Claire Bennett <claire@finapps.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Urgent: spike in 5xx/429s — impacting FinApps payments

Vanessa — APPROVE the temporary reroute to your hosted pool. We will also immediately raise conntrack limits on our firewall and extend NAT ephemeral port ranges. Please proceed and ping me when the reroute is in place so our ops team can validate.

We appreciate the rapid response — please keep Marissa involved on compensation if this extends past the window.

Claire
Claire Bennett
